reason: The text demonstrates Hebrew people actively expressing their views in multiple contexts. They shout publicly in support of the new king ('Let the king live!' - יְחִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ), engage in dialogue and ask questions, and even those who oppose (the 'sons of Belial') openly express their contempt and criticism. Samuel addresses the assembled people and explains matters to them. Throughout the narrative, various individuals - Saul, servants, Samuel, the people - all speak freely and exchange views. There is no evidence of discouragement from expressing opinions; rather, the people are depicted as vocal and participatory.
